about: CHAIN coast_watch_810 (Design/content/chains/coast_watch_810.md): the emperor's coast watch and Godfred's two hundred ships, 808 to 812. Fourteen cards. The count at Dorestad calls boats and men to the watch on the river mouths (s01); the watch post at Walichrum is four boats, two of them barges (s02); in the Danes' harbours every rope-walk is sold out (s03); a Frisian mound can be warned (s04); the fleet is seen at sea (s05); the mound at Emuthon must find its part of the hundred pounds (s06) and a Dane weighs it on the strand with his own weights (s07); the emperor's host eats the river bare and his elephant dies at Lippeham (s08); the emperor's envoys ask where the watch was (s09); in the hard winter three men want the boat for three different springs (s10); the old Roman light at Bononia is lit again (s11). Three endings: the emperor's ships at Ganda (end_fleet), the thing on the mound at Emuthon (end_islands), the oath on the Eider (end_eider). Progress is flags ch_coast_watch_810_1 to _11; the branch flags, the three end flags, the grand rewards and the three 'changed_' flags are listed in the chain page. The spine's flags gf_warned and gf_paid_share (thread godfreds_market) are set here. Only s01 and s10 are needed to reach an ending; every other step is optional and colours what the endings offer. Cards are drawn on a call at their port in their months and years, so the waits are the real ones of 810 and 811. The forge names the people; the words call them Count Folcbert (cast.folcbert), Gerwin, Sibrand, Tetta, Sibo, Ketil and Baldric (invented, attested name parts); the Dane among the crew is cast.crew.ravn. The words are in Data/writing/chain_coast_watch_810.json; each option's note names the writing key of its outcome text. Sources in the notes and the chain page: Annales regni Francorum 800, 808 to 811; Einhard, Vita Karoli 14, 17, 22, 32; MGH Capitularia I nos. 34, 46, 48, 51, 64, 74. Written 6 Oct 2026; a draft for the user to overwrite.

cards.note: Step 1, the start: Dorestad, 808 to May 810, drawn on a call there once the house has made two calls. Count Folcbert (cast.folcbert, invented man in a real office) has the order read: ships and a watch on the river mouths. Sources: Charles sets up a fleet and posts guards on the coast of the Gallic sea, March 800 (ARF 800; chronicle 800-03-channel-coastguard); 'de navigia praeparando circa litoralia maris' (Capitulare missorum of 802, MGH Capit. I no. 34 c. 13a (?)); the ships ordered built, 808 (MGH Capit. I no. 51 c. 9-10; chronicle 808-march-land-sea); stations and watches at every port and river mouth (Einhard, Vita Karoli 17); of the poorer Frisians six equip a seventh for the host (Memoratorium of 807, MGH Capit. I no. 48 c. 3 (?)). Reric burned 808 (ARF 808); Count Egbert at Esesfeld, March 810 (ARF 809). Sets ch_coast_watch_810_1 and one of _roll, _paid_seventh, _aside.

cards.note: Step 2 (optional): Walichrum, at the mouth of the Scheldt, from step 1 until June 810, drawn on a call there. The watch as it was: Einhard says stations and watches were set at all the ports and river mouths where ships could enter (Vita Karoli 17); what such a post looked like is not recorded, so the four boats, the beacon pile and the commander Gerwin (Ger- + -win) are INVENTED. The man who is 'the seventh part of a soldier' is the Memoratorium of 807 again. That the watch could see a fleet and not stop one is what 810 showed. Sets ch_coast_watch_810_2 and one of _stood, _letter.

cards.note: Step 3 (optional): Ripa or Sliesthorp, 809 to May 810, drawn on a call there. The king's men gather ships (spine thread godfreds_market, hooks ripa and sliesthorp). Sources: two hundred ships from Nordmannia (ARF 810); Godfred counted Frisia and Saxony as his own provinces and boasted he would soon come to Aachen (Einhard, Vita Karoli 14); he had sent word to the emperor by merchants in 809 (ARF 809), so a merchant asked whose man he is fits. What the fleet bought and where it gathered is not recorded: the rope and bread are INVENTED. The Dane of the crew is cast.crew.ravn, who 'knows men in that fleet and says less than he means' (spine). Selling bread to the king's buyers breaks no capitulary (the ban of 805 is on arms and mail) but a count would mind. Sets ch_coast_watch_810_3 and _word; _sold_fleet.

cards.note: Step 4 (optional): a Frisian landing (Emuthon, Doccinga, Wijnaldum or Medemelacha), March to June 810, drawn on a call there. The warning. Real: the fleet ravaged all the islands off the Frisian shore (ARF 810); the sun was eclipsed on 7 June 810, a Friday three weeks after Pentecost (ARF 810; chronicle 810-06-07-solar-eclipse). INVENTED: that anybody warned them. Sets the spine's flag gf_warned ('he brought warning of the fleet to a Frisian port before it came') and changed_frisia_warned_810: the mound's cattle are inland and its best silver hidden when the ships come, so the fights go no better but the Danes carry less away. No sea dykes yet in 810, so the word goes from mound to mound by boat and on foot at low water. Sets ch_coast_watch_810_4.

cards.note: Step 6: Emuthon, June 810 to May 811, drawn on a call there. The hundred pounds (spine thread godfreds_market, hook emuthon; realms/frisia_lotharingia.md card 2). Source: the fleet 'fought three battles with the Frisians, and the Danes, being victorious, laid a tribute on the conquered, and a hundred pounds of silver had already been paid by the Frisians' (ARF 810, in our own words). A hundred pounds is 24,000 pennies. How it was shared out is not recorded: a part for each mound, four pounds for Emuthon, is INVENTED. Emuthon in 810: a trading mound on the Ems with large ewe flocks and wool cloth, no church yet; Bant off the river mouth; the nearest chapel Liudger's at Leer (dossiers/emuthon.md). Buying a needy man's goods far under their worth is 'foul gain' in the capitulary of Nijmegen, 806 (MGH Capit. I no. 46 c. 15-17 (?)). The cattle plague of 810 killed the oxen (ARF 810). Sibrand (Sib- + -brand) and Tetta are invented. Sets ch_coast_watch_810_6 and one of gf_paid_share (the spine's flag), _cheap, _ferried.

cards.note: Step 7 (optional): Emuthon, June and July 810, after step 6, drawn on a call there. The weighing on the strand. Real: tribute by weight of silver (ARF 810); folding balances and lead weights are common finds in the North of this age, and the Danes' ounce was not the Frankish one; Godfred stayed at home and boasted he would come to Aachen with a great host (Einhard, Vita Karoli 14; ARF 810). INVENTED: Ketil (a common Danish name), the twelve roped men, the quarrel over the weights. That Frankish pennies went into the pan as plain silver: coin was weighed, not counted, in the North before about 825 (BRIEF rule 2). Sets ch_coast_watch_810_7 and one of _ransomed, _true_weight, _boast.

cards.note: Step 8 (optional): Dorestad, Noviomagus or Diusburg, June to September 810, drawn on a call there. The emperor's host (spine hooks dorestad and diusburg). Sources: at the news Charles sent out to gather the host, crossed the Rhine at Lippeham and waited there for his troops, and 'the elephant which Aaron, king of the Saracens, had sent him died there suddenly'; he camped where the Aller meets the Weser; there he heard that the fleet had gone home and that Godfred had been killed by one of his own following (ARF 810, in our own words). Lippeham lay about the mouth of the Lippe, a day below Diusburg (?). The cattle plague that killed nearly all the host's oxen (ARF 810), and the rumour that men of Duke Grimoald of Benevento went about with a poison dust (Agobard, De grandine 16). Three months' food carried from the march: the Boulogne capitulary, 811 (MGH Capit. I no. 74 c. 8), set down a year later (?). The provisioner is unnamed. Sets ch_coast_watch_810_8; _fed_host.

cards.note: Step 9 (optional): Dorestad, September 810 to February 811, drawn on a call there. The emperor's envoys on the coast. Sources: the news of the fleet reached Charles at Aachen (ARF 810); the capitulary of 810 for the missi sent out that year has a head 'on timber for building ships' (MGH Capit. I no. 64 c. 16; chronicle 810-fleet-ordered-810); 'the emperor had ordered a fleet built the year before' (ARF 811); ships built on the rivers of Gaul and Germany that run into the northern sea (Einhard, Vita Karoli 17). INVENTED: that the envoys held a hearing at Dorestad and what was said. It is modelled on what the next emperor did after Walcheren fell in 837, when he held an inquiry at Nijmegen into those he had set to guard the coast and it was found that the Frisians' disobedience had made the defence impossible (Annales Bertiniani 837, in our own words). Telling the truth costs the goodwill of Count Folcbert, who holds the house's debt. Sets ch_coast_watch_810_9 and _told_truth or _blamed.

Sources: a very hard winter, the frost shutting the roads between Franks and Danes, so that the peace Hemming asked for could only be sworn on weapons until spring (Annales Xantenses 810; ARF 811); in spring twelve men of each people met on the Eider (ARF 811), led for the Franks by Count Wala, son of Bernhard; ships built for the fleet at Ganda (ARF 811). The fleet road is always open; the islands road needs step 6; the Eider road needs something the Danes know you by, or their tongue.

cards.note: Step 11 (optional, the fleet road): Quentovic, August to November 811, drawn on a call there. Sources: in the autumn of 811 the emperor went to the sea town of Bononia (Boulogne) to look at the fleet he had ordered built the year before, 'and he restored the lighthouse set up there in old times to guide the course of sailors, and had a fire lit on its top by night' (ARF 811, in our own words; chronicle 811-10-boulogne-lighthouse); the capitulary given at Boulogne orders that whenever a fleet is sent the lords themselves go aboard and be ready for it (MGH Capit. I no. 74 c. 11; chronicle 811-10-boulogne-capitulary). Boulogne is a day's sail north of Quentovic and is not a port of the game, so the card lies at Quentovic. The seasick lord and the harbour man are INVENTED. Sets ch_coast_watch_810_11; _piloted, _saw_light.

cards.note: ENDING 1, the emperor's ships: Ganda, September 811 to the end of 812, drawn on a call there. Flag ch_coast_watch_810_end_fleet. Sources: from Boulogne the emperor 'came to the river Scheldt, to the place called Ganda, and looked at the ships built for that same fleet', and was back at Aachen about the middle of November (ARF 811; chronicle 811-11-ghent-ships; dossiers/ganda.md); he was tall, and in his last years limped a little on one foot (Einhard, Vita Karoli 22). How many ships, and where on the bank, nobody knows (dossiers/ganda.md): thirty hulls, the green oak, the spare keel and the wright Baldric (Bald- + -ric) are INVENTED. What really happened is the plain road: lords were ordered aboard (Boulogne capitulary c. 11), the fleet is not heard of again, and in the 830s nobody watched the coast. The hard road (needs the truth told at the inquiry, and a turn on the watch, the roll or the warning) is history changed: changed_coast_watch_frisian, a watch of sworn Frisian shipmen paid in toll freedom, with a duty that lasts (ch_coast_watch_810_watch_duty). Grand rewards: unlock_ship_north_sea_merchant_ship; or unlock_charter_dorestad and unlock_title_emperors_man; or unlock_title_counts_shipman.

cards.note: ENDING 2, the mound: Emuthon, May 811 to the end of 812, drawn on a call there (also the road for a house that did step 6 and then missed the winter card: from September 811). Flag ch_coast_watch_810_end_islands. Real: the peace sworn on the Eider in spring 811 (ARF 811); the Frisian law-speaker, the asega, and judgment at the people's meeting (Lex Frisionum; lore/law_tolls.md); Louis gave the Frisians back their right of inheritance in 814 (Astronomer, Vita Hludowici 24 (?)). INVENTED: the thing after the shearing and what it offers; Sibo, Tetta's grandson (a Frisian short name). What really happened is the plain road: the coast paid, mended, and was raided again (Chron. Moiss. 813). The hard road (needs the warning or the ransom, and not the cheap cloth) is history changed: changed_frisian_beacons_811, the mounds from Bant to the Lauwers swear a watch of their own with a fire on each, three hundred years before the sworn Frisian districts are heard of (?). Grand rewards: unlock_plot_emuthon; or unlock_factor_emuthon; or unlock_plot_emuthon and unlock_kin_fosterling_sibo.

cards.title: The thing on the mound
cards.intention: The shearing is done and the mound holds its meeting on the green by the creek. Peace has been sworn on the Eider. The oxen are dead and the wool is good.

cards.note: ENDING 3, the oath on the Eider: Sliesthorp, March 811 to the end of 812, drawn on a call there. Flag ch_coast_watch_810_end_eider. Sources: 'the peace announced between the emperor and Hemming, king of the Danes, was only sworn on arms because of the hardness of the winter, which closed the road between the parties, until with the return of spring twelve nobles of each people met on the river Eider and confirmed it by oaths given in turn, each after his own rite and custom' (ARF 811, in our own words). The Franks: Count Wala son of Bernhard, Burchard, Unroch, Uodo, Meginhard, Bernhard, Egbert, Theotheri, Abo, Osdag, Wigman; the Danes: Hemming's brothers Hankwin and Angandeo, Osfrid called Turdimulo, Warstein, Suomi, Urm, Osfrid son of Heiligen, Osfrid of Sconaowe (Skane), Hebbi, Aowin (ARF 811; the spellings vary). Hemming died that winter and the kingdom was fought over in 812 (ARF 812); the peace was sworn again in 813 (ARF 813). The Eider is a day's ride south of Sliesthorp (?). INVENTED: the spokesman, the Saxon interpreter, and Ketil turned trader. What really happened is the plain road: the oath named no merchants. The hard road is history changed: changed_eider_peace_merchants, the clause that traders of both realms cross with their goods and buy and sell in peace, which the Danes and Franks really agreed only in 873 (Annales Fuldenses 873). The other chain lost_brother has its own clause (changed_eider_peace_captives); the two do not clash. Every road here sets ch_coast_watch_810_danes_man: at Dorestad the count counts you a Dane's friend. Grand rewards: unlock_charter_sliesthorp; or that and unlock_title_danish_guest_right; or unlock_partner_ketil.
